name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Article 14 of the Law on Citizenship applies fully gender-neutral rules: a child acquires Uzbekistan citizenship at birth if both parents (or the single parent) are citizens, or if one parent is a citizen and the other is stateless/declared absent/a foreign citizen. Establishment or recognition of paternity or maternity by an Uzbek-citizen parent confers citizenship on the child regardless of place of birth.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate or paternity/maternity recognition document

sources.title: ecoi.net -- hosted text of the Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan 'On Citizenship,' Article 14 (descent-based acquisition) and Article 8 (marriage does not change citizenship)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Uzbekistan). STATUS: DRAFT -- ecoi.net hosts the primary legal text itself (the Law 'On Citizenship,' Article 14), not a secondary summary, but this dataset's validator requires tier-1 (government-hosted) sourcing for hard requirements to publish, and a lex.uz (Uzbekistan's own government legislation portal, confirmed tier-1 elsewhere in this build for the 2021 procedural decree) copy of the same Law was not directly located in this search pass -- worth a follow-up to pull it from lex.uz directly and upgrade this file. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING: descent citizenship is fully gender-neutral on its face -- no paternal-preference asymmetry of the kind found in Iran, Kuwait, or Syria's descent laws built elsewhere in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed left null for a child born to one citizen and one foreign parent -- Uzbekistan is widely understood to restrict dual citizenship generally (see uz_citizenship_naturalisation.json's explicit renunciation requirement for naturalizing adults), but no source in this build directly addressed how that applies to a child acquiring citizenship by descent while also holding a foreign parent's nationality, so it is not asserted here.
